messages:
maya: Quick check — planning a canary to move service 'feature-proxy' from ClusterIP + ALB TLS termination -> NLB TLS passthrough (NodePort). Want to avoid double-TLS and keep probes stable. Any gotchas?
sam: Main things: ensure Service type=NodePort and targetPort matches pod readiness port. NLB health uses nodePort if targetType=NodePort. Also consider externalTrafficPolicy=Local if you need client IP.
linh: Also watch SNI — with passthrough the Gateway forwards raw TLS. Gateway must be set to TLS mode=Passthrough and SecretBinding used for certs.
oliver: If using Gateway API, TLS listener config looks like:
```
kind: Gateway
spec:
  listeners:
  - protocol: TLS
    mode: Passthrough
    port: 443
```
SecretBinding must reference the cert secret in gateway namespace (or use serviceAccount RBAC to read).
sam: Terraform note: annotate svc for NLB + set type NodePort. Example snippet: 
```
resource "kubernetes_service" "feature_proxy" {
  metadata {
    annotations = {
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type" = "nlb"
    }
  }
  spec { type = "NodePort" }
}
```
maya: Healthchecks — our app expects TLS handshake + HTTP/2 ALPN. With passthrough, LB can't do L7 checks. Should we switch to TCP healthcheck to avoid failing probes?
linh: Yes, switch to TCP (or TCP-SYN) on the NLB side and use a readinessProbe tcpSocket on the container port. That avoids requiring TLS handshake for the LB.
oliver: Rollout pattern: create a new Gateway/Route that points 10% to the canary backend (or use a separate service and shift weights). Keep the ALB route as an emergency fallback so rollback is quick.
sam: PR opened: https://git.company/infra/feature-proxy-nlb-canary — includes TF, k8s manifests, and docs about healthchecks. @marco can you review the Gateway SecretBinding + RBAC parts?
marco: on it. I'll validate secret namespace, ServiceAccount perms, and the gateway listener config.
maya: Thanks — planning to start the canary tomorrow 09:30 PT. tagging @ops-oncall in case auto-scaling surprises. :thumbsup: 
ops-oncall: noted, I'll be available during the rollout window and watching node CPU / NLB error metrics.
infra-bot: Canary deployment job queued: job/feature-proxy-canary-244999 will run at 2026-03-18T16:30:00Z 
maya: one last Q: any specific metrics we should closely watch beyond p95 latency? 502/504 spikes?
linh: Yes — p95 latency, 5xx spikes (502/504), and node CPU across NodePort-serving nodes. Also keep an eye on connection churn and conn.tracker metrics on the NLB side.
maya: perfect, will post results and quick rollback notes in this thread after the window ends. Thanks everyone.
